implications_for_gold: C2-C5: supports 'match'. This is the first execution of the shipped R analysis; reference_recomputed can be filled with the values above (provenance: direct execution of shipped R with one path edit, scope: original analysis on deposited data), and the not_checkable alternative is no longer needed on evidence grounds. C1: contradicts the current cause text. The shipped cleaning script, with three lossless path edits (R4), regenerates the deposited Data_cleaned.csv exactly and yields 11,016, the printed value, under R 4.6.1. So R version does not explain the report's 11,018. The remaining dependency question is genderdata: it is not on CRAN and not in the deposit; it was installed from GitHub at commit df16017, the commit the authors' script comment names. Two readings for the gold owner: (a) if installing a named non-CRAN dependency at the authors' stated commit counts as dependency installation, C1 -> 'match', reference_recomputed 11016, cause cleared; (b) if only what is inside the pinned package counts, C1 stays not_checkable but the cause should read 'gender-inference data (genderdata) not deposited; with the commit named in the authors' code the printed 11,016 recurs'. In either case, keep the report's 11,018 as a non-scoring source_report diagnostic and note that it did not recur with gender 0.6.0 and genderdata df16017 under R 4.6.1, so the report's attribution to R/gender version is unconfirmed here. Paper level: 'computationally reproducible' is supported for all five claims, including from raw data. The existing 'computational issues' alternative now rests only on the script stopping at the Table 1 stargazer() call under current R. That error occurs after estimation and affects no printed number, and whether it warrants the alternative is the gold owner's call. requires_human_rerun can be cleared or reworded (this run was by an agent, not a human); label_confidence can rise.
notes: Both analysis runs stop with 'the condition has length > 1' at the Table 1 stargazer() call (line ~200). Traced to stargazer 5.2.3's internal .inside.bracket(), which fails under R >= 4.2 when a multi-model call deparses to several lines; a single-model or two-model call works. This is a dependency/R-version incompatibility in table formatting, not in estimation: all six Table 1 models are fitted before the error, and the claim values come from the fitted felm objects. Script content after Table 1 (later tables and figures) was not executed; no edit was made to get past the stargazer call because that would go beyond R4. The cleaning script ran to completion (exit 0; 5,834/5,834 episodes parsed; 63,320 rows written). Full logs and downloads stay in /tmp/scratch_gold2/claude/G-26 (not in the repo).
